# Make the completion-verification close gate survive a large, legitimate ticket

Retyped from `bug` to `task`: the original report ("the close gate blames a missing `agents`
extra") was a real defect and its messaging half has LANDED (change 1027, and change 1060 now
extends it to the step-budget path). What remains is not a misbehaviour to correct but a
deliberate re-shaping of how the gate handles size — a design change with rejected alternatives,
which is task-shaped work.

## What is now PROVEN (measured this session, not inferred)

Repro target: ticket `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56`, whose work is complete and merged, and which still
cannot close.

1. **Context size was never the binding constraint.** 9fd4's assembled context is **34,282 chars
   ≈ 8,570 tokens** (reproduced byte-for-byte against the live failure). The verifier runs
   `claude-sonnet-4-6` (~200k-token window), so the ticket is ~**4%** of the window and the old
   24,000-char bound is ~**3%**. The bound is a self-imposed cost guard, not a capability limit.
2. **The advertised remedy could not work.** Composition: description 10,281 + 9 comments 23,617
   (comments = 69%). Deleting the ENTIRE description still leaves **24,001 chars — one over the
   old limit**. Comments are the only sufficient lever, and the store is append-only:
   `_lib_writes` exposes `comment()` with no delete/redact counterpart.
3. **The two bounds were incoherent.** Criteria ⊂ description ⊂ context, yet
   `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` (32,000) > `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` (24,000). Proven by sweep: criteria
   totalling 26,000–31,900 chars pass every criteria bound and are then refused on context — the
   top quarter of the advertised criteria budget was unreachable.
4. **The real blocker for 9fd4 is the STEP budget, not context.** At default settings the primary
   verifier exhausts `max_iterations=480` after ~780s and raises a plain `LLMError`. Recovery is
   gated on `_is_token_exhaustion(primary_exc)` (`completion_recovery.py:549`), so a step-budget
   exhaustion **never enters recovery at all** — the compaction path is unreachable for the very
   ticket that motivated it.
5. **The messaging fix works live.** The gate now says "The completion verifier ran and then
   failed, so this is not a missing install or credential — act on its own reported remedy…".

## Approach

**Compaction must be a last resort, not the primary mechanism.** Change 1060 currently makes
compaction the normal path at a 40,000-char budget. That is the wrong shape: shipped ticket 19b1
makes ticket **comments** the sanctioned completion-evidence channel ("the verifier reads the
ticket's comments so documented evidence is incorporated on the next verification"), so eliding
oldest-first comments can drop exactly the evidence that proves a criterion and flip a PASS to a
FAIL. Since 8.5k tokens was never expensive, the budget should be grounded in real model
capability so elision essentially never fires for a realistic ticket, with compaction retained
only as a guard ahead of the hostile-input refusal.

**And the actual dead end must be removed:** recovery exists because "the aggregate verifier could
not finish" — 9a08 names the intended remedy as "bound/compact evidence and tool output … or
recover by splitting the decision step". A step-budget exhaustion is that condition, so it must
reach recovery rather than terminating the close.

**Alternative rejected — escalate to a larger-context model as the fallback.** Tempting, but it
solves a constraint that is not binding: nothing here is near a context window (4% of it). It does
not address either real limit (tool-call iterations; the separate 16,000 output-token budget), and
`completion.py` records a measured reason it would likely make things WORSE — the framework default
(opus) was rejected for this gate because it "over-explores … blowing the step budget", which is
precisely the live failure. It also makes a signed verdict tier-dependent: the same ticket could
pass on one model and fail on another, which is a worse property for an attestation gate than for
a plain reviewer.

**Alternative rejected — tell authors to prune tickets.** No such policy exists anywhere in the
repo predating this bug's own error string, and (2) above shows pruning cannot even work for a
comment-dominated ticket.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — budget grounded in model capability;
  compaction demoted to last resort; recovery entered on step-budget exhaustion, not only token
  exhaustion.
- `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — remedy selected by cause
  (LANDED in 1060; keep).
- `docs/llm-framework.md` §"Bounded completion recovery" — document the budgets and why.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py`.

## Testing

Unit tier with a fake runner (no billable calls) for every bound and branch, plus one live
end-to-end close of 9fd4 as the acceptance oracle. Mutation-verify each new test by re-introducing
the exact mechanism it pins.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a completion-verifier failure that is NOT a missing dependency (specifically a step-budget
      exhaustion, which ran the model) does not tell the operator to install the `agents` extra or
      set an API key, and does surface the remedy the exception itself carries; a genuine
      unavailability STILL gets the install-the-extra guidance (negative control)
- [ ] the recovery context budget is derived from stated model capability rather than a round
      number, and a ticket the size of 9fd4 (34,282 chars) is verified with NO material elided —
      a test asserts the full context reaches the model for a realistic ticket
- [ ] compaction, when it does fire, never drops an acceptance criterion, marks every elision
      in-band so the model cannot mistake a partial context for a whole one, and is covered by a
      test asserting both properties
- [ ] a step-budget exhaustion of the primary verifier reaches bounded recovery instead of
      terminating the close, and a test pins that entry path (it is currently gated on token
      exhaustion only, so this is the mechanism that makes 9fd4 uncloseable)
- [ ] `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` cannot exceed the context budget — pinned as an invariant test,
      so the incoherence that made the top quarter of the criteria budget unreachable cannot
      return
- [ ] a genuinely unbounded payload still fails fast with ZERO billable recovery calls, asserted
      by call count, so relaxing the budget does not delete the cost guard
- [ ] ticket `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56` closes at DEFAULT settings without `--force-close` and without
      any `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS` override, with the command output recorded as a comment here —
      the end-to-end proof that the reported problem is actually resolved
